about: Which versions of each part may talk to which (SECURITY-HARDENING-PLAN.md 18.13). `minimumSecurity` is the lowest version that is still safe; `preferred` is what a release run ships. They are different numbers on purpose: raising the first locks old parts out, and it is only raised when an upstream security fix or a protocol break needs it. `current` is what this tree builds. `receiverFirst` lists the parts that must be able to VERIFY a new format before any part starts ISSUING it, in the order to deploy. An unknown version of a signed format is refused, never read as the older broad authority.

recovery-record.note: v1 rows are read-only legacy until their owner re-enrols

webapp-shell.note: the service worker replaces an older shell on the next load

receiverFirst: boot worker and .com verify the format
web shell, then iOS and Android store builds that issue it
